prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a narrow locker-room scene where a masked person in a 'BANGKOK' hoodie stands on the right within arm's reach (roughly 0.4–0.6 m from the camera wearer), holding a smartphone at chest-to-waist level just 0.3–0.5 m in front of and slightly below the camera. To the left and 0.5–1.5 m behind the foreground person, a person in a white 'JAMES 10' jersey bends forward facing away toward a bank of lockers on the far left (which enters the foreground at 0.3–0.6 m in frames 3–5), while two to three additional people stand further back in the corridor at roughly 1.5–4.0 m. Across the five frames, the foreground person stays within arm's reach and turns their torso slightly toward the camera in frame 4 before the camera wearer's own hand reaches onto their left arm in frame 5, while the 'JAMES 10' person retreats from about 1.0 m in frame 1 to 1.8 m in frames 3–5 as the camera shifts left next to the lockers. The depth map clearly separates the foreground person's extended hands and phone from their torso and the angled locker wall—a continuous distance gradient that is harder to judge in RGB alone—while showing that the foreground person's upper head and lower body are cropped out of view and that they partially occlude the background people. However, the depth map is unreliable in the deeper background (beyond 2 m), where the corridor walls, blue door, and distant people merge into nearly uniform black, and in frame 3 where the foreground person's left shoulder and neck appear overly saturated at the same brightness as the closer left hand.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the people and held object in the locker room, consistently segmenting the foreground person on the right (at 0.4–0.6 m, facing left and slightly toward the camera while looking down at their phone rather than at the camera wearer) whose head above the nose and body below the hips are out of view. In frames 1–2, it separates the person in the white jersey on the left (1.0–1.5 m away, facing away and bending down) and two to three background people standing 0.5–1.5 m behind them (at 2.0–3.5 m from the camera, facing variably toward or away from the camera), before the foreground person and lockers occlude most of the background crowd in frames 4–5. Within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the foreground person is the held smartphone (0.3–0.5 m away, positioned left of the foreground torso and below head level), which lowers slightly in frame 4 and rises again in frame 5 as another hand touches the foreground person's right-side sleeve. Compared to RGB, the masks make it easier to count distinct overlapping individuals in the dim background of frame 2, though the map completely omits static structural elements like the nearby lockers on the left and the distant walls. The segmentation is unreliable in several places: it misses the phone entirely in frames 1, 4, and 5, mislabels the phone as a 'bottle' overlapping a 'cell phone' in frame 2, misclassifies the bent-over 'JAMES 10' person's torso as a 'backpack' in frame 3 and misses them completely in frames 4–5, and merges the foreground person's hands with the phone or torso.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map tracks joint locations on a black background, showing mostly the foreground person's left hand in the lower-left to center-left region (0.3–0.5 m from the camera wearer, within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the foreground person) as it holds and taps the smartphone across all five frames. As the sequence progresses, that magenta hand skeleton shifts from the lower left in frame 1 toward the center in frames 2–3, drops to the bottom edge in frame 4 when the arms lower, and returns to the lower center in frame 5 alongside a second magenta hand skeleton on the lower right (about 0.3 m away from the first hand) where a hand reaches onto the foreground person's arm. In frame 3, a yellow upper-torso rectangle and head keypoints appear in the upper-left quadrant for the person in the white jersey (about 1.5–1.8 m away and 1.0 m behind the foreground hands), capturing their forward-bent, downward-facing orientation away from the camera wearer. This map reveals exact finger articulation and hand orientation—such as the splayed fingers hovering over the screen in frames 2–3 and the grasping fingers on the sleeve in frame 5—even when motion blur and skin-on-skin contact make joint positions ambiguous in the RGB frames. However, the pose map is highly unreliable overall: it completely fails to detect the foreground person's torso, head, and right hand across all frames (likely due to heavy close-range cropping and occlusion), misses all background people in frames 1, 2, and 4, and hallucinates a distorted yellow body skeleton entangled with the foreground hands in frame 5.
